subject: 20260913-183723-sweep-deepgram-30-5234
headline: The agent held its typical reply speed up to 40 calls at once, and the thing to fix first is the closing thank-you turn: its slowest replies stall at every load, and those stalls made the 5-call step the run's only failure.

insights.title: The closing thank-you turn stalls at every load, and those stalls made the 5-call step the only failure
evidence: refund-hesitant, step baseline, turn 5: ttfa p50_ms 735.2, p95_ms 3166.9
refund-hesitant, step c40, turn 5: ttfa p50_ms 734.8, p95_ms 3116.2
refund-hesitant, step baseline: endpointing p99_ms 387.4, think_speak p99_ms 2922.4
refund-hesitant, step c5: verdict fail, p95_ratio 2.04, ttfa p95_ms 1939.9
refund-hesitant, step c5, turn 5: ttfa p90_ms 3190; turn 2: ttfa max_ms 1283
refund-hesitant, steps c10, c20, c40: p95_ratio 1.32, 1.04, 1.08
refund-hesitant, calls log turn 5: heard_cut_short 6, ttfa_p50_ms_cut_short 775.5, ttfa_p50_ms_heard_in_full 735.2
insights.finding: The wait before the agent starts speaking (ttfa) behaves oddly on the last turn, where the caller says "Alright, that works. Thanks for sorting it out." Its median (p50, the typical turn) is the lowest of any turn in each step. Its p95, the slowest 5% of turns, lands between 3116.2 and 3594.2 ms at every step. That includes the baseline, where only one call ran at a time, so load does not create the stall. At baseline the slow end sits in thinking up the reply (think_speak p99 2922.4), while noticing the caller stopped (endpointing) stays at 387.4. The 5-call step (c5) is the only step that failed, and its slow end did not grow with load: c10, c20 and c40 all came back close to baseline. Within c5, turn 5 has a p90 of 3190, while no other turn passed 1283 ms. So c5's 3177.1 ms endpointing stall can only have fallen on the closing turn. At that step, some closing stalls were in hearing the caller stop, not only in thinking. Mishearing does not explain it: on this turn the median barely moves between callers heard in full and callers cut short.
insights.why_it_matters: This one short goodbye turn produces the worst waits in the run, and it happens with a single caller. Adding servers will not fix it. It also means the c5 failure is most likely not a capacity problem. Reading it as one would send the team after the wrong fix.
insights.next_step: Pull the traces for every turn-5 reply at baseline and c5 whose ttfa passed 2000 ms, and check whether the time went to endpointing, to the model's first token, or to the speech engine's first audio.

insights.title: The task-success judge passed 200 of 210 calls, so the quality verdict cannot show quality slipping under load
evidence: refund-hesitant, judge misses: both criteria missed 0 of 210
refund-hesitant, step c40: wer mean 3.3%, worst 100.0%, deletions 179, substitutions 6, insertions 2
insights.finding: An AI judge grades whether each call did the job, using two criteria. It passed 200 of 210 calls, and neither criterion failed once. It also passed all 8 calls where the agent's transcript misheard the caller. At c40, the agent's hearing lost a whole turn's words at worst (word error rate, or WER, worst 100.0%), and nearly all errors were dropped words (179 deletions). Even so, the task still counted as done. Every step's quality verdict is pass, but it rests on criteria this agent never failed.
insights.why_it_matters: A check that never fails cannot tell the team when quality starts to give way as calls increase. The pass at c40 tells us little about whether busy periods hurt the caller's outcome.
insights.next_step: Add a judge criterion the agent could plausibly miss, such as "The assistant tells the caller how long the refund takes to reach their card", then rejudge this run's calls.

insights.title: No capacity limit was reached by 40 calls at once, but the first turn and the network show early strain there
evidence: refund-hesitant, step baseline: ttfa p50_ms 781.8; step c40: ttfa p50_ms 784.7
refund-hesitant, step c40, turn 1: think_speak_p50_ms 526.7; turn 4: think_speak_p50_ms 512.9
refund-hesitant, step baseline, turn 1: think_speak_p50_ms 472.6; turn 4: think_speak_p50_ms 497.3
refund-hesitant, step baseline: transport_rtt p99_ms 90.8; step c40: transport_rtt p99_ms 110.3, max_ms 185.1
insights.finding: At 40 calls at once, the typical wait matches baseline, and ttfa p95 stays below Coval's published 2000 ms load line. That line is another company's target, not this team's. The test stopped before finding where the agent breaks. Small signs appear at c40. Within c40, the opening turn has the slowest median thinking time. Within baseline, the opening turn is faster than turn 4. One possible cause is many calls opening together. The network round trip's p99, the slowest 1%, is higher at c40 than at baseline. The single slowest thinking time in the run also falls at c40.
insights.why_it_matters: The team knows the agent holds at 40 calls at once, but not how much headroom remains. The first signs of strain are in the opening turn and the network, not in the median a dashboard would show.
insights.next_step: Rerun the ramp with steps above 40 calls at once, and watch the turn-1 think_speak median and the transport_rtt p99 for the first step where they keep climbing.
